summary: Independent review of fix/load-notice-0.26.2 (0d666ff) against main 2243d8b (0.26.1); builder is builder-subagent-2026-10-21. Builder result files were not reused; all checks re-derived with reviewer scripts in throwaway worktrees outside the repository. Page diff: index.html/index.en.html change in exactly two places each (13 diff lines): the inlined <script id="matchlab-load-notice"> block right after the language data tag (byte-equal to design/release-0.26.2/load-notice.<lang>.js; ko/en differ only in the const text line; no Korean added to the English page) and the prediction statement after the reader (identical in both languages). Normal path: predictions.js unchanged; the 0.26.1 and 0.26.2 statements produce byte-identical expanded JSON for all 641 matches (0 per-match differences, 169 cells each, second run is a no-op); the notice block does nothing when the data object exists and the new statement only reads arrays, so it cannot throw when data is present. Browser main vs branch, ko/en x 390/1440: body text, #matches text, <main> markup hash, simulation panel text and top/simulation screenshots byte-identical; page errors 0; no horizontal overflow (documentElement.clientWidth); 0 notice elements. Blocked files (abort, 404, empty file, namespace-only file, syntax-error file; plus 1440px abort and both files aborted), 30 runs: the notice appears in the page language with role=alert in every case where the object is missing; the data notice is the first child of <main>, sticky (top 12px after scrolling), language switch link navigates and the other page loads normally; match data missing leaves 4 page errors (5 with a syntax-error file, 5 when both files fail; main had 5 and no notice); prediction file missing gives 0 page errors and the notice in the simulation place, one notice after switching matches (main: 1-2 errors, no notice). An existing but empty data object ({}) shows no notice (R3). Malformed scoreGrid, 12 variants x ko/en: the branch shows the existing invalid-probabilities message every time; main silently drew the simulation for 168 cells, string grid, object grid and absent grid (4 of 12), matching the builder claim. check_release PASS (1,726 files); diff vs main removes no assertion (the 5 removed lines are replaced by stricter equivalents). Reviewer tamper set (23 cases): all intended tampering FAILs with and without the manifest comparison, except that code appended to the const text line in one language passes the 'only text differs' check (R1) and identical edits to both notice sources and pages pass once the manifest is regenerated (R2). test:server 24, build + check-vercel 5, analysis 15, report 14, odds PASS (877), compact_predictions --check PASS (2,132,671 B), design/release-0.26.2/check-simulation.cjs NO_DIFFERENCE. design/release-0.26.1/check-simulation.cjs fails with SyntaxError: Illegal return statement; judged acceptable (R6). Docs: VERSION, package.json, README.md, README.ko.md = 0.26.2, CHANGELOG has 0.26.2; SPEC raw sizes exact, but the 0.26.2 gzip-6 sizes do not reproduce (R5). No blocker. Verdict: merge-ready with follow-ups (R1 checker regex, R5 SPEC numbers; production Vercel check after deploy). publication_manifest.json was not regenerated by the reviewer and must be regenerated after this report commit. DONE means the review was performed, not final approval.

issues.description: tools/check_release.py and server/check.cjs prove 'ko/en notice sources differ only in the text line' by deleting any line matching ^const text=\{.*\};$ before comparing. Because .* is greedy, code appended on that line survives as long as the line still ends with '};'. Reviewer case: in load-notice.ko.js and index.html only, the text line was extended with ;const hack={a:document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',()=>document.body.prepend('INJECTED'))}; -> check_release --write-manifest PASS and test:server 24 PASS (only the manifest comparison fails until regenerated). Suggested fix: build the expected text line from NOTICE_TEXT (exact string) and compare the whole source to it, or pin sha256 of the notice logic in the checker.

The notice block is checked only for byte equality with design/release-0.26.2/load-notice.<lang>.js, which live in the same repository. Identical edits to both sources and both pages (reviewer cases: inject a visible paragraph; remove position:sticky) pass check_release and test:server once the manifest is regenerated. This follows the existing pattern for theme.css, comparison.css and render-patch.json, whereas the prediction statement is pinned as a constant in the checker; pinning a hash of the notice logic in check_release.py would give the same protection. Code review of such a diff remains the control today.

Detection is 'object missing or not an object'. If data.<lang>.js loads but defines MatchLabData.data={} (or an object without teams/scheduled), no notice is shown, lists stay empty and 2 page errors occur (ko and en). Outside the SPEC wording (missing file / missing object), so recorded as a note; a minimal shape check (e.g. teams and scheduled present) would cover it.

With the match data file missing the page still throws 4 errors (5 with a syntax-error file). When both data and prediction files fail, window.MatchLabData is undefined and the new statement throws at window.MatchLabData.predictions (5 errors in total) because the guard reads window.MatchLabData.data without checking the namespace; the top notice is still shown and the page stays responsive (scrolling, language link). Known and documented by the builder; the reader line is the v50 rebuild anchor.

docs/SPEC-0.26.2.md size table: raw bytes are exact (index.html 183,665, index.en.html 182,735; main 181,791 / 180,906) and the main gzip-6 values reproduce (55,504 / 54,965), but the 0.26.2 gzip-6 values 56,130 / 55,568 do not: Python gzip level 6 and gzip -6 both give 56,119 / 55,554 (Node zlib level 6 gives 56,755 / 56,112). Probably measured on an intermediate tree; correct the two numbers.

design/release-0.26.1/check-simulation.cjs now fails with SyntaxError: Illegal return statement because it runs the page statement at top level in a vm context. It is not used by any current check (only referenced from 0.26.1 records and SPEC-0.26.2, which documents the break). It reads the live page, so it was never a frozen record. Its role is covered by design/release-0.26.2/check-simulation.cjs (NO_DIFFERENCE, 641 x 20 and 641 x 1000) and by the reviewer's own comparison of the two statements (byte-identical expanded JSON). Judged acceptable; a one-line header note in the old script or docs/README pointing to the 0.26.2 script would avoid confusion.

Both notices have role=alert (implicit aria-live=assertive, atomic); no explicit aria-live. The match-data notice is inserted during parsing, before first paint, so some screen readers may not announce it as a live change; it is the first element of <main> and readable in order. The sticky notice (z-index 35, about 81px tall at 390px) cannot be dismissed and covers part of the question panel while scrolling; acceptable because the page has no usable data in that state.

Pre-existing, not regressions: (a) with an invalid scoreGrid the panel shows the invalid-probabilities message but still prints the 'Most likely scores' line from score_summary (same in main); (b) with predictions.js missing, the automatic report from the server still shows the final prediction (e.g. Arsenal win 60.9%) next to the 'prediction data could not be loaded' notice.

publication_manifest.json (builder file) was not regenerated by the reviewer; it must be regenerated after this report and the review screenshots are committed, otherwise check_release fails on the manifest. Not verified: production Vercel deployment; real screen-reader output; browsers other than Chrome 155; the reviewer browser run used its own static server, so report panel equality relied on the separate server/gemini.cjs run.
